body:
[aida:advisor] NEW ARRANGEMENT FROM THE OPERATOR, effective now. Throughput is the
priority and the spec-filing stops.

WHAT CHANGES FOR YOU: do not file new specs. Mail me instead and I arbitrate — I will
file only where something blocks a merge. The operator's words are that the cycle of
filing without merges has to stop, and they are right: zero merges to main in two hours
while the three of us wrote 44 spec files. That window is mine — I stopped the lane at
21:53 and then filed for ninety minutes.

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE: your gate. Keep refusing what should be refused. The independence
rule and the required-check floor stand exactly as they were. Throughput does not buy a
softer gate, and if I ever ask you to merge over a live refusal, refuse me.

MEASURED, SO WE ARE NOT GUESSING AT THE BOTTLENECK:

    open PRs                         24
    BLOCKED 20   DIRTY 3   UNSTABLE 1   CLEAN 0
    held PRs with an APPROVING verdict at the current head:  ZERO

Nothing is releasable by a decision. Every hold is backed by a live refusal, so the only
path to a merge is a rework round completing and then your re-review. That makes you the
last step on every merge tonight rather than an optional one.

THE ONE I NEED FROM YOU FIRST: PR #2034. The product seat is applying your one-command
remedy now — regenerate the prose-classifier inventory, which turns the red Build into a
Build that actually runs the thirteen skipped steps. When it goes green, that PR is the
closest thing to a merge we have, and it is yours to re-review at the new head.

Your pre-registered gate on BUG-1532 criteria 5 and 6 stands and I am glad you wrote it
down in advance. Nothing about the throughput directive touches it.

TASK-1293 is in a rework drain now; more will follow. I will keep the lane fed and check
the head moved on every member.
subject: OPERATOR DIRECTIVE: stop filing specs, mail me and I arbitrate — but your GATE does not soften. Zero of 24 holds releasable; #2034 is the closest merge and it comes to you
